markdown_report:
**Recommendation:** Run the predefined three-condition GRU4Rec study with matched supervision and candidate construction. At 30% progress, this remains a feasible experiment if measured runtime permits all conditions. Its contribution is controlled evidence rather than novel cropping; no validation improvement is established.

**Insights from the starting point**

1. All four padding audits pass their declared tolerances. Preserve the corrected recurrence; these checks support execution consistency without establishing gradient or predictor-export equivalence.
2. Removing older context decreases mean training margins in every category, although less than removing recent context. Older history can therefore help; suffix removal also increases target distance, limiting that comparison.
3. Electronics has an 8.85% negative-wins rate and 20.72% small-margin rate. These identify sampled training difficulty, not validation ranking quality or evidence of current intent.

**Insights from related work**

1. [TimeSHAP](https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.00073) motivates prefix perturbations. [DA4Rec](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.11136v1) and [sequence-splitting research](https://arxiv.org/html/2604.05309) establish supervised cropping precedents and motivate separating context from supervision coverage.
2. [Sampled-metric research](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) distinguishes sampled from full-catalog rankings. Keep pinned host HR@10 for selection; interpret simulator recommendations separately.
3. [Gating analysis](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v119/gu20a.html) motivates complementary recurrent diagnostics. Gate saturation alone establishes neither forgetting nor historical usefulness.

These insights organize three directions: controlled context regularization, attribution of historical influence, and evaluation validity.

**Framework**

| Condition | Input context | Supervised positions | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | Full | All baseline-valid | Reference |
| B | Full | Planned suffix | Supervision control |
| C | Planned suffix | Identical planned suffix | Context intervention |

C−B compares training-context interventions with matched supervision; B−A compares supervision policies. These are conditional training-procedure comparisons, not causal estimates of user intent. Candidate membership, weighting, reduction and updates must also match B/C.

**Candidate ideas** — O/P/D denote originality, potential and implementation difficulty, each 0–10; higher D means harder. Scores are qualitative.

| Idea | O: positive / negative | P: positive / negative | D: positive / negative |
|---|---|---|---|
| Matched suffix training | 3: informative control / cropping precedents | 7: resolves confounding / uncertain gains | 5: unchanged backbone / candidate-gradient care |
| Prefix-order diagnostic | 3: targeted control / standard perturbation | 6: tests order dependence / artificial histories | 3: inference only / rank ties |
| Lag-gradient and gate panel | 3: complementary evidence / established tools | 6: explains sensitivity / local attribution limits | 6: no new model / recurrent instrumentation |

**Selected algorithm**

Freeze per-row cropping probability 0.5; retain a uniformly sampled length from ceil(n/2) through n, otherwise all n events. Preserve chronological adjacency, original target alignment and differentiable full-context prefix states in B.

```python
plan = suffix_plan(sequence, dedicated_rng_seed_42)
mask = baseline_valid & plan.retained_positions
candidates = baseline_candidate_plan(original_batch)
B_loss = complete_retained_loss(GRU(sequence), candidates, mask)
C_loss = complete_retained_loss(
    GRU(zero_removed_prefix(sequence, plan)), candidates, mask)
```

Train conditions separately from the supplied cold start. Match candidate IDs/multiplicities, corrections, negatives, target weights and complete per-query losses before reduction [GRU4Rec](https://hidasi.eu/assets/pdf/gru4rec_v2_cikm18.pdf). Verify loss/gradient agreement on a tiny fixture. Predeclare affordable E≤200, 200 batches/epoch, final checkpoints and A>B>C ties within the shared budget. Select the complete condition by four-category macro validation HR@10; deploy one checkpoint/category with full histories. Report category discordances and paired user-bootstrap intervals only when host per-user hits exist. Intervals exclude seed variability and adaptive-selection optimism [Cawley–Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v11/cawley10a.html). Full-history inference mismatch and popularity shortcuts remain hypotheses; freeze the winner before held-out evaluation.

idea.description: A controlled three-condition study of stochastic old-prefix removal in corrected GRU4Rec: unchanged baseline A, full-context suffix-supervised B, and cropped-context identically suffix-supervised C. Match retained queries, candidate construction and complete loss reductions between B and C. Select one complete condition using pinned four-category macro validation HR@10.
idea.motivation: User feedback suggests overly broad historical influence, but measured prefix removal usually reduces training margins. Matching supervision and candidate construction separates the context intervention from target coverage and cross-example loss coupling. Supervised cropping already has precedents; the contribution is a reproducible controlled experiment, with no demonstrated validation gain.
idea.implementation_notes:
Preserve the supplied corrected GRU4Rec backbone, loss family, optimizer, sampler and predictor architecture. The actual training implementation is not supplied here: verify its candidate construction, reduction and regularization before applying masks, rather than assuming an elementwise loss. Use preprocessing seed 0 and training seed 42. Freeze a common affordable epoch count E<=200 before observing scores, exactly 200 batches per epoch, and final-epoch checkpoints. Measure costs before committing to the complete experiment. All training, diagnostics, debugging and failures count toward 43,200 GPU-seconds; four concurrent slots do not enlarge that allowance. Each run remains single-GPU. Report incomplete comparisons explicitly.

Each condition independently trains one model for each required category from the supplied corrected cold start; never load another trial's checkpoint. Deploy only the selected condition, exactly one checkpoint per category, without averaging or fusion. Retain Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl routing, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], and trial-local artifacts.

Freeze and replay identical original batch, negative and cropping plans for B/C using separate seed-42 RNG streams. Keep model initialization, optimizer steps, loss weights and schedules identical. Generate plans for A through the separate stream as well, without changing its baseline training inputs or supervision. Equal seeds do not guarantee identical dropout draws across executions; document this limitation and preserve dropout configuration.

For n>=1 real input events, crop with probability 0.5 and draw k uniformly from ceil(n/2)..n inclusive; otherwise k=n. The policy can retain all events even on the crop branch, so report actual changed-row counts and retained-length distributions. Empty rows contribute no supervised targets. C zeros the removed prefix in place and retains original suffix positions. B retains every input but supervises the same retained suffix positions. A keeps baseline supervision. Never shift targets into their own causal inputs. Leave B's earlier recurrent states differentiable through suffix losses; detachment would introduce another intervention.

Distinguish query rows from candidate columns. Construct B/C candidate plans from identical original batches before filtering supervised queries. Preserve candidate IDs, order, multiplicities, duplicate-target exclusions, positive-index mappings, padding masks, sampling corrections, candidate weights and any loss-specific score penalties. Removing a query's direct loss must not automatically remove its target from other retained queries' candidate pools. Removed input occurrences receive no input-path gradient in C, while their item embeddings may still receive candidate-side gradients. Dropped query logits receive no direct loss gradient; full-context prefix states in B can still receive gradients through retained suffix losses.

Compute complete finite per-query losses on eligible retained queries, then reduce with the same declared rule in B/C. Use a retained-valid-target token mean if that is the baseline reduction; if the baseline uses per-row or per-user means, preserve and explicitly document those weights instead. A loader row is not necessarily a unique user. Keep parameter regularization and optimizer weight decay separate from query masking. For BPR-max, negative-only softmax weights and its score penalty belong inside each query loss; TOP1-max also uses negative-only weights. Neither requires another division by negative count. Sampled CE uses its own positive-plus-candidate normalization. Do not replace the supplied objective with one of these losses merely because it is discussed here.

Verify reduction axes, candidate masks before softmax/logsumexp, positive remapping, duplicate targets and padding on a tiny deterministic fixture. Compare dense valid-query masking against gathered-query computation for loss and parameter gradients. Avoid multiplying invalid NaNs by zero. Preserve the baseline policy for empty-negative queries; if unspecified, define and document a finite exclusion policy consistently for B/C. An all-masked batch must skip backward and optimizer.step, including weight decay; replayed plans make B/C skip the same batches. Record scheduled batches and actual optimizer updates separately. Check causal target alignment, finite gradients and retained candidate-side gradients. These targeted checks are necessary because a superficially correct loss mask can change the objective.

Keep packed padding-skipping recurrence and reset state per independent history. Inference uses the full baseline-truncated permitted history and greatest nonpadding position, never count-1; preserve the baseline empty-history policy. Verify checkpoint and embedded predictor-writer feature/score agreement on fixed fixtures. No architectural change is proposed. Cropped training followed by full-history inference creates a plausible distribution mismatch, not an established failure. Retain the predefined full-history deployment policy in the primary experiment. Any later truncated-inference comparison must be declared as an additional validation configuration, count toward search breadth, and score each model separately without fusion.

Retain ModelView.model as the actual nn.Module, item_emb, aligned B x L x H log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data and review_data. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), returning measured metrics with metric_definitions and restoring model mode. Consume (None, sequence, positive, negative) batches with B x L tensors. Report paired matched-suffix margins, changed/unchanged rows, valid-position counts, token exposures and GPU seconds as training diagnostics. These are not validation HR@10. The passing padding audit does not prove export or gradient equivalence.

Use only permitted histories, titles, descriptions and timestamps. Ratings, review text, item categories, prices, stores and simulator traits are unavailable despite generic upstream examples. Interactions and description overlap do not establish ownership, compatibility, purchase need or current intent. Generate required full-catalog unseen-item recommendations for five real training users per category; keep these separate from sampled host selection.

Keep splits, evaluator, evaluation seed 42, 200 validation users/category and 99 unique negatives unchanged. Select one whole condition by host macro validation HR@10, with A>B>C for exact ties. Do not mix category winners across conditions in this predefined study. If host per-user hit outcomes are available, compare conditions on identical candidate pools using d(c,u)=hit_X(c,u)-hit_Y(c,u); report category differences and X-only/Y-only hits. Independently resample users with replacement within each fixed category, preserving paired outcomes, and recompute the equally weighted macro difference for 10,000 seed-42 bootstrap replicates. Report percentile 95% intervals. Do not infer these intervals from aggregate HR alone or resample the four fixed categories. One additional hit changes category HR by 0.5 percentage points and macro HR by 0.125 percentage points; this is resolution, not a significance threshold.

Intervals describe user-sampling uncertainty conditional on fitted models, seed, splits and fixed candidates, assuming independent users within categories. They exclude training-seed variability, alternative negative samples and adaptive-selection bias. Report all tested conditions and configurations; treat small gains as exploratory. If making prespecified multiple hypothesis tests, declare the test family and apply an appropriate correction such as Holm; ordinary winner-bootstrap intervals do not correct selection optimism, and intervals crossing zero do not demonstrate equivalence. Popularity, history length and user-specific shortcuts may persist after cropping. Freeze the chosen model before the host's final held-out evaluation. No full-catalog gain, seed robustness or accuracy improvement is currently established.
idea.pseudocode:
predeclare crop policy, affordable E<=200, 200 batches/epoch,
final-epoch checkpoints, baseline loss reduction, and tie order A>B>C
verify tiny-fixture candidate mappings, masking, finite losses and gradients

for condition in [A, B, C]:
    for category in four_required_categories:
        initialize supplied corrected GRU4Rec with training seed 42
        initialize independent deterministic sampler and crop-plan RNG streams
        for epoch in range(E):
            for step in range(200):
                original_batch = baseline_sample_batch()
                sequence, positive, negative = unpack(original_batch)
                valid = baseline_valid_target_mask(original_batch)
                candidates = baseline_candidate_plan(original_batch)
                # Preserve IDs, multiplicities, positive mappings, exclusions,
                # sampling corrections, weights and loss-specific penalties.
                retained = zeros_like(valid)
                for row in batch:
                    positions = chronological_nonpadding_positions(sequence[row])
                    n = len(positions)
                    if n == 0: continue
                    crop = crop_rng.random() < 0.5
                    k = randint_inclusive(ceil(n/2), n) if crop else n
                    retained[row, positions[-k:]] = True
                inputs = sequence.clone()
                query_mask = valid if condition == A else valid & retained
                if condition == C:
                    inputs[(sequence != 0) & ~retained] = 0
                features = model.log2feats(inputs)
                # B retains differentiable prefix states; do not detach.
                queries = gather_eligible_queries(features, query_mask)
                query_candidates = select_query_mappings(candidates, query_mask)
                # Select query mappings without shrinking shared candidate pools.
                queries, query_candidates = apply_declared_empty_negative_policy(
                    queries, query_candidates)
                if no_eligible_queries(queries):
                    record_skipped_update()
                    continue
                per_query_loss = complete_baseline_loss(queries, query_candidates)
                loss = declared_baseline_reduction(per_query_loss)
                loss = add_baseline_explicit_parameter_regularization(loss)
                baseline_optimizer_step(loss)
                record_targets_tokens_updates_and_runtime()
        save final checkpoint and consistent predictor artifacts under trial directory
        verify trained-model/exported-predictor agreement on fixed fixtures
        run family-compatible measured diagnostics and required user recommendations
    obtain unchanged host macro validation HR@10 for complete condition

report all complete condition scores and category outcomes
if host paired per-user hits are available:
    report discordant hit counts
    bootstrap paired users within each category for 10000 seed-42 replicates
    recompute equal-category macro differences and percentile intervals
select highest-scoring complete condition with predeclared A>B>C ties
export exactly one checkpoint per category from that condition
predict with full permitted history and greatest nonpadding-index readout
freeze selection before host final held-out evaluation; never fuse scores

originality.positive: Matching supervision, candidate coupling and loss reductions makes the cropping comparison scientifically interpretable within this GRU4Rec benchmark.
originality.negative: Supervised cropping and sequence-splitting ablations have direct precedents. The proposal contributes experimental control rather than a novel augmentation mechanism.

future_potential.positive: The experiment can distinguish useful context regularization from supervision changes and provide a reusable protocol for recurrent recommendation studies.
future_potential.negative: Older context currently helps average sampled margins. Validation gains, inference-length robustness and transfer beyond seed 42 remain unestablished.

code_difficulty.positive: The intervention preserves the GRU architecture and deployment interfaces, largely changing input masks and supervised-query selection.
code_difficulty.negative: In-batch candidate coupling, complete loss penalties, reduction semantics, gradient reach and predictor consistency require more care than simple elementwise masking.

related_work.title: TimeSHAP: Explaining Recurrent Models through Sequence Perturbations
contributions: Provides event-level perturbation attribution and older-prefix pruning for recurrent models.
Motivates investigating historical influence while keeping the prediction endpoint fixed.
limitations: Its original application does not establish recommendation gains on these Amazon datasets.
Inference perturbation attribution does not establish the benefit of training-time cropping.

related_work.title: Sampling-reliability study, RecSys 2025
contributions: The supplied search summary distinguishes sampled evaluation reliability from agreement with full evaluation and preference alignment.
limitations: Does not establish gains from the proposed GRU4Rec intervention.
The pinned host evaluator remains the required selection criterion.

related_work.title: Recurrent gating analysis, Gu et al., ICML 2020
contributions: Analyzes recurrent gating, information retention and optimization.
Supports interpreting gate statistics alongside perturbation measurements.
limitations: Gate saturation alone cannot establish forgetting or historical usefulness.
Does not directly validate the proposed Amazon recommendation experiment.

related_work.title: GRU4Rec: Recurrent Neural Networks with Top-k Gains for Session-based Recommendations
contributions: Introduces ranking objectives including BPR-max and TOP1-max with negative-only softmax weighting.
Clarifies why candidate membership and loss-specific score penalties must be preserved in matched experiments.
limitations: The supplied corrected baseline's actual objective must be inspected before applying loss-specific implementation advice.
Does not establish the benefit of stochastic prefix removal.

related_work.title: GRU4Rec reference implementation
contributions: Provides implementation details for candidate weighting and GRU4Rec losses.
Supports checking normalization and regularization semantics.
limitations: An unpinned repository link may change.
The host baseline may differ; this implementation must not silently replace host behavior.

related_work.title: DA4Rec, WWW 2024
contributions: Distinguishes target-preserving perturbations, including cropping, from transformations that change prediction targets.
Provides precedent for direct supervised augmentation without a contrastive objective.
limitations: Does not establish the exact proposed matched-supervision protocol.
Its findings do not guarantee gains on the four pinned Amazon tasks.

related_work.title: Pay Attention to Sequence Split
contributions: Separately varies sequence splitting, supervision coverage and loss choices, including GRU4Rec.
The supplied summary reports negligible or adverse splitting effects under multi-target CE, motivating supervision controls.
limitations: Does not isolate the exact stochastic suffix-retention policy proposed here.
Does not establish harm specifically from cropped GRU training followed by full-history inference.

related_work.title: CL4SRec: Contrastive Learning for Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Uses contiguous subsequence cropping among augmentations for paired sequence views.
Combines next-item prediction with a contrastive objective.
limitations: Its crops need not retain the latest suffix.
The proposed supervised-only intervention does not implement its contrastive objective; cropping alone offers little novelty.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Explains limitations of sampled ranking metrics, including disagreement with full-catalog model rankings.
limitations: Identical candidate pools enable paired comparisons but do not remove sampled-evaluation bias.
Does not authorize correcting or replacing the pinned host evaluator.

related_work.title: Statistical Significance Tests for Machine Translation Evaluation
contributions: Provides a paired bootstrap precedent that can be adapted to paired recommendation hit outcomes.
limitations: The proposed category-stratified recommendation bootstrap is an adaptation.
Intervals require per-user outcomes and do not capture training-seed or adaptive-selection uncertainty.

related_work.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains selection optimism from repeatedly optimizing against finite validation data.
Motivates reporting search breadth and freezing selection before held-out evaluation.
limitations: Ordinary bootstrap intervals around a selected winner do not correct adaptive selection.
A single fixed-seed experiment cannot establish training-seed robustness.

related_work.title: Recency Sampling for Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Discusses training/evaluation task mismatch for BERT4Rec, providing related motivation to examine deployment consistency.
limitations: BERT4Rec masking mismatch is not evidence of the same failure in GRU4Rec.
Any inference-length experiment here requires a separately declared validation configuration.
